title: Let Us See If the Vine Flourish
summary: This is the inspection. The withdrawal has done its work; the soul and the Lord now walk together through what has been cultivated, surveying growth. The teachings begin with the cycle now turning peacefully through the heavens without breaking them, and the threefold register of what is named; they proceed to the garments worn in life and death, the appointed time when light came, the building of the dwelling; the molding of Adam, the senses arrayed as rooms in a city, the lifespan diminished by stages; the three compassions and the four weepings; the hidden and manifest members in the Lord's outgoing, the Divine Human clothed in the elements, the three rocks of glory, what love and hatred truly are; the three things shown to Adam, the seven goods of light, the two mysteries of sun and night; the Ambassador's daily rising and setting, the five works of fire (love), the twelve zodia bound in the sphere; and at last the cosmic body in its full anatomy, the chain of inward gathering, and the names of the garments collapsing back into one likeness at the end. What was contested is now reviewed in its growth.
organizing_principle: The teachings treat the same divine outgoing the earlier sections narrated, but now from the vantage of fruit rather than contest. The cycle that was binding is now the cycle that does not break the heavens. The names that were structures of seeking are now registers of recognition — gods, rich-men, angels. The garments that were stripped are now seen for what they conjoin. The body that was bound is now the body whose senses are rooms, whose fivefold structure cannot stand if one degree is missing, and whose lifespan diminishes by stages — anticipating the fivefold completeness named at the section's end. The compassions and weepings are not new wounds but the divine sorrow now seen as part of the work. The hidden and manifest members of the Lord's outgoing, the Divine Human clothed in the elements, the rocks of glory — these are foundations the soul can now stand upon. The next teaching distinguishes love from hatred at their cosmic origin — love as the bond of the Greatness, hatred as the first death of the self that has claimed itself — a definition that could not have been received in the second state but can be received now. The teachings then set out the three things shown to Adam, the seven goods, and the two mysteries; then the Ambassador's daily round, the five works of fire, the zodia bound; and they close with the cosmic body, the inward gathering, and the names returning to one. The section is the parallel treatment of what was in contest, now in cultivation. What was the contest's wound is now the field's harvest.
